reviews.summary: Round-1 repairs were checked against the working tree. Most are correct: the native terminate is non-blocking and the IsProcessInJob error is fixed; the containedSession done path awaits 'emptied' and every refusal/launched/stop path calls markEmpty; the codex app-server probe, process.server.ts (owned env hardening still applied) and TaskManager.launch/approve refusal are in place; restartSurvivorRefusal is scoped to the same mission or task; the settleStops and dispose ordering has no deadlock; and the native build proof matches the current C source. Incomplete repairs: RESTART-03/startup-throw (R2-01) and STOP-2 (R2-02) are partial, and SHUT-1 (R2-04) misses the failOperation path. Also found: an alias-stat regression in interpreter resolution (R2-03, not executed) and unguarded bookkeeping in terminateJob (R2-05). No BYPASS or escape from the job was found. The round-1 C1 close-drop was left as an accepted LOW and was not re-opened.

repairVerdicts.note: Not changed in close_group. Accepted LOW per the disposition: the last-handle close is KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, and provider terminateJob keeps the handle until the kernel reports 0. Reviewed and unchanged, as the task stated.
native/bunny-owned-process.c:161-162 now uses GetLastError() when IsProcessInJob fails and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED only when member is FALSE.

Partial. terminate_owned now calls terminate_group(g,0) and returns at once, and JS polls. close_group still blocks the Node main thread for up to 1.5 s plus a writer wait (up to about 3.4 s). Residual, not a containment bypass.

verification.server.ts exec runs an absolute PATH-resolved interpreter, excluding task-folder entries, inside runWindowsOwnedProcess with owner verification.python. Residual regression in resolveInterpreter (R2-03): statSync on App Execution Alias stubs.

codex-probe.server.ts containedTransport runs the app-server in an OwnedProcessGroup with interactive stdin (spawn arg true), and probe() routes win32 through runWindowsOwnedProcess. A containment failure rejects the probe. Interactive budget (512 KiB) is checked before WriteFile.
runProcess always uses runWindowsOwnedProcess on win32. spawnSession's spawnChild seam is only a test seam (production never passes it). The owned env hardening is still applied when owned is set.
containedSession done awaits the emptied promise, which resolves only on kernel zero or the refused/empty paths. Retry is unconfirmed-only with backoff. Residual bookkeeping-throw gap in R2-05.

Partial. The launched:true marker is attached only when terminate() returns normally (owned-process-group.server.ts:178-181). If terminate() or persist() throws after launch, the root is reported as refused with admitted=false (R2-02).
stopContained text distinguishes admitted/never-admitted, prints 'an unknown number of' when terminatedAtEnd is null, and the Stop text no longer claims a job for a never-admitted session.

Partial. http close awaits settleStops() before db.close, and dispose() runs after it. The failOperation path (manager.server.ts:321) calls session.stop() outside stopsInFlight, so shutdown does not await it (R2-04).
terminate is non-blocking (terminate_group(g,0)) and the JS retry polls with backoff. close_group still blocks on the main thread, which is accepted as residual latency at shutdown and finalize.

manager.server.ts possiblyAlive treats unknown birth as possibly alive; no-identity records go to cleanup_unverifiable and markProviderSessionReview, and 'empty' is never claimed without a verified absence.
possiblyAlive gives a liveness predicate (null/NaN birth counts as alive) used by reconcile, separate from the strict kill-authority identity match in terminateVerified.

Partial. The per-record parse is in try (owned-process-group.server.ts:106-110), but field shape is not validated and reconcile runs unguarded in the constructor (manager.server.ts:185, 235-236). See R2-01.

restartSurvivorRefusal is checked in the private launch path used by both approve and approveDelegated (manager.server.ts:1150), and matches only the same mission or task. Unrelated work is not blocked.
Same residual as RESTART-03. The constructor still throws for a parseable record whose launcherPath or members are missing or invalid (R2-01).

rows.title: Restart reconcile dereferences unvalidated record fields outside any try, so a parseable malformed record aborts TaskManager construction
rows.reproduction: Write runtime/provider-sessions/<uuid>.json containing {"schema":"bunny-owned-operation/1","operationId":"<uuid>","containment":"running","closed":false} (no launcherPath, no members). readProviderSessions (owned-process-group.server.ts:106-113) accepts it because only schema, containment and operationId are checked. Then the TaskManager constructor calls reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions (manager.server.ts:185) with no try, and line 235 evaluates record.launcherPath.split(...) and line 236 record.members.map(...), which throw TypeError. The Host constructor fails and the Host does not start. Only the JSON parse is inside the try (owned-process-group.server.ts:107-110), so the round-1 RESTART-03 / R1-LOW-startup-throw repair is incomplete.
rows.rootCause: Validation covers the parse and three header fields. The shape of launcherPath, launcherPid, members and each member is never checked, and the reconcile step that consumes them runs unguarded in the constructor.
rows.repair: Validate the full shape in readProviderSessions' try (launcherPath string, launcherPid number, launcherCreatedAt number, members array of {pid:number, createdAt:number, file?:string}) and route failures to unreadable. Also wrap each record's reconcile call in try/catch that holds the record as unreadable and emits provider_session.unreadable. Add a constructor test with such a record asserting the Host still starts and the record stays held.

votes.reasoning:
Not refuted. Verified in the code:

1. src/lib/bunny-host/owned-process-group.server.ts:106-113 (readProviderSessions). The try block (lines 107-110) checks only schema, containment and operationId. A record with no launcherPath or members passes. Because the record has closed:false, it is pushed into `recovered` and persisted as interrupted/closed (line 114), and it is returned without a shape check.

2. src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:184-185. The TaskManager constructor calls readProviderSessions then reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions(found.records) inside `if (this.dataDirectory)`. An awk scan of lines 115-190 found no try/catch enclosing that call. Only the nearby holdUnreadable path is wrapped, and that wrapper is in the later check() closure, not the constructor.

3. manager.server.ts:235-236 (per the finding's line numbers, in reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions). `record.launcherPath.split(...)` throws a TypeError when launcherPath is undefined. The members .map also throws when members is missing. Nothing in that function guards against it, so the constructor throws and the Host does not start.

4. The record is persisted before the throw, and a later boot still selects it (containment "running" is not in the skip list at line 111). So the failure repeats on every start until someone deletes the file by hand.

Reachability is limited. The app's own writers always set launcherPath and members (owned-process-group.server.ts:156 and 190), and persist() writes through a tmp file and rename, so a normal crash does not produce this shape. It needs a hand-edited or externally damaged file in the data directory. That is fail-closed (no process is killed or trusted, and nothing is bypassed), so the impact is a Host availability failure, not a containment bypass. LOW is the justified severity. The finding's reproduction and root cause are accurate, and its repair is consistent with the code.

Not refuted; the mechanism is real but the trigger is local tampering only. Verified in code:
- owned-process-group.server.ts:101-113 (readProviderSessions): the try covers JSON.parse and only checks schema, containment and operationId. A parseable record missing launcherPath/members is pushed into `recovered` unchanged, and the state is persisted as interrupted/closed (line ~114) before the caller runs.
- manager.server.ts:~173-176: the constructor calls reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions(found.records) with no try. Inside it (~line 234-236) the array literal evaluates record.launcherPath.split(...) and record.members.map(...) unguarded, so a missing field throws TypeError and the constructor fails. The claimed reproduction holds.
- The consequence is a repeated boot failure: the record is still containment "running" on the next start (the skip filter at line 107 only drops empty/absent_after_restart/refused), so it is recovered and throws again until the file is deleted by hand.
- Trigger reachability is narrow. The only writer (owned-process-group.server.ts:156 constructor, plus members push at line 190) always writes launcherPath and members, and persist is whole-file JSON, so a truncated file fails the parse and goes to the unreadable hold path. A parseable file missing those fields requires out-of-band edits to the local runtime directory, which is the same trust level as the Host itself. Nothing in the viewer, phone or network path reaches it.
- Hence a real robustness gap (fail-start rather than hold), not a silent containment bypass. Failing loudly at startup does not leave an unkilled process unaccounted for. The R2-01 repair (validate shape inside the try, and guard each record's reconcile call) is still appropriate. Severity LOW is justified. The native/README has no out-of-contract entry that covers this, so it is not a documented exclusion.

rows.title: Post-launch inspect failure is reported as never-admitted ('refused', admitted=false) when terminate() or persist() throws
rows.reproduction: The root is launched and runs. The first post-launch inspect() calls persist(), which can throw EPERM on the rename (Windows antivirus or indexer lock). The catch at owned-process-group.server.ts:178-181 then calls this.terminate(), which calls persist() again. If that throws too, the raw error escapes without Object.assign(...,{launched:true}). In adapters.server.ts containedSession (lines ~348-364) the error is not 'launched', so the code runs group?.close('failed') and settles state 'refused' with admitted:false and detail 'Containment unavailable — execution refused'. The job was killed by the close, but the record and Stop text claim no provider process was ever admitted. Round-1 STOP-2 said only a launch that never produced a handle may be 'refused'.
rows.rootCause: The launched marker is attached only when terminate() returns normally. Any exception from the bookkeeping path inside the catch bypasses it, so the classification depends on which I/O call failed instead of on whether the handle exists.
rows.repair: In OwnedProcessGroup.spawn, attach launched:true to every error thrown after this.handle is set, whatever its origin, for example by wrapping the post-launch block in try/catch that rethrows Object.assign(error,{launched:true}) whenever this.handle is non-null. Let terminate() failures in that path fall back to close() and keep the handle. Add a test where persist throws after launch and assert state is not 'refused' and admitted is true.

votes.reasoning:
The defect is real but narrow, and the record-level part of the claim is overstated.

Mechanism, verified in code:
- owned-process-group.server.ts:175-180: the post-launch catch calls this.terminate() and attaches launched:true only if terminate() returns normally.
- owned-process-group.server.ts:203-207: terminate() calls this.native.terminate(...) first, then persist(). If persist() throws (writeFileSync/renameSync EPERM from an antivirus or indexer lock, realistic on Windows), the kernel job has already been terminated, but the raw error escapes the catch without the launched marker.
- adapters.server.ts:346-363: the outer catch sees no launched flag, runs group?.close("failed") inside a swallowing try, then settles state "refused" with admitted:false and "Containment unavailable — execution refused". The root did run, since native launch resumes it before inspect() is reached at line 177.

Consequences:
- The in-memory containment snapshot (and the detail/admitted fields it feeds) reports that no process was admitted. manager.server.ts:1897 then appends "No provider process was admitted for this session." This is the untruthful statement the finding describes.
- The persisted record is not the "refused" state the finding claims. close() at owned-process-group.server.ts:196-197 rewrites containment to "empty" or "unconfirmed" because its value is "running", not "refused". The record claim holds only if the close persist also fails.
- If close's persist also throws, the exception is swallowed by adapters.server.ts:357, and release() (line 200) is never called. That leaves the tracked group registered, a minor leak the finding does not mention.

Nothing elsewhere prevents this. The only trigger is an I/O failure on the bookkeeping write after the root has already launched, so impact is limited to misleading status text and bookkeeping. The job is still killed and no process survives. Suggested repair is right: mark the error launched whenever this.handle is set, and let terminate() failures fall back to close() while keeping the handle.

The defect is real as stated, but its impact is classification only, not a containment escape.

Code path, verified by reading:
- owned-process-group.server.ts spawn(): the post-launch try block runs this.inspect(); persist(). On failure the catch calls this.terminate() and then throws Object.assign(..., {launched:true}) only if terminate() returns normally. terminate() calls persist() whenever record.containment is set, which is always true for provider sessions. If that persist throws (for example an EPERM rename on a Windows-locked file), the raw error escapes the catch without the launched marker.
- adapters.server.ts containedSession (about lines 344-364): an error without launched:true goes to group?.close("failed") and settles state "refused", admitted:false, detail "Containment unavailable — execution refused". The root did run, so the record and Stop text misstate the outcome.

Why it is LOW and not higher:
- The job is not leaked. containedSession calls group.close("failed") in the non-launched branch, and close() releases the handle, which with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates every member. The other callers (runWindowsOwnedProcess and the codex probe) also call close() in their catch blocks. No process escapes.
- The trigger needs two persist failures in sequence (inspect's persist only runs when something changed, then terminate's persist), so it is rare.
- The consequence is a truthfulness and classification error (admitted:false for a root that ran), with a recorded containment of empty or unconfirmed rather than refused. No lost accounting for a live process.
- Partial mitigation: close() still records activeProcesses from the native close return, so the count is kept.

The proposed repair (mark launched:true whenever this.handle is non-null, and let terminate failures fall back to close while keeping the handle) is sound. I found no prevention elsewhere that would refute it.

rows.title: Interpreter resolution uses statSync, which fails on Windows App Execution Alias stubs, so Python-via-alias verification now fails (regression)
rows.reproduction: On a Windows machine where python.exe is available only as the Microsoft Store alias in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps (an APPEXECLINK reparse point), resolveInterpreter calls statSync(candidate) on that PATH entry. libuv opens the file without FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, so the call throws (ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE, surfaced as UNKNOWN or EACCES). The catch on line 19 skips it, resolveInterpreter returns null, and exec throws 'No Python interpreter on PATH outside the task folder.' The pre-change execFile('python') used CreateProcess PATH search, which launches the alias, so verification worked before. Not verified by execution in this session.
rows.rootCause: Existence is tested with a stat that follows the reparse point. App execution aliases are not regular files that stat can open, so they are dropped.
rows.repair: Treat a candidate as present when lstatSync succeeds (or accessSync with X_OK succeeds), and do not require isFile() for APPEXECLINK reparse points. Keep the task-folder exclusion. Add a Windows regression with a fake alias-style stub, or document the alias limitation if it is intentionally unsupported.

votes.reasoning: Code-grounded check of src/lib/bunny-host/verification.server.ts. Line 19 is exactly `try {if(statSync(candidate).isFile()&&!inside(root,canonical(candidate))) return candidate;} catch { /* not here */ }`, and resolveInterpreter (line 13) skips any candidate whose statSync throws. Nothing elsewhere in the file or resolveInterpreter's callers (runPython, line 26) adds a fallback to a PATH-search launch, so when python.exe exists only as a WindowsApps App Execution Alias and no other python is on PATH, runPython throws "No Python interpreter on PATH outside the task folder." (line 27). That is a real false negative, not a bypass: it fails closed. I did not verify the libuv/Node behavior by execution (the rules forbid running anything), so the statSync-throws-on-APPEXECLINK premise rests on known Windows reparse-point behavior, not a test. Not refuted: the defect is real in principle but narrow (alias is the only interpreter, and a Store python is installed behind the alias), and it changes availability of verification, not containment. Severity LOW is justified. Suggested repair from the finding (lstatSync existence check, or an X_OK-style check, keeping the task-folder exclusion) is reasonable, and a Windows regression test with an alias-style reparse stub would confirm it.

Not refuted, but unverified by execution and the impact is narrow.

What I confirmed in src/lib/bunny-host/verification.server.ts (lines 13-23 of the working tree): resolveInterpreter tests each absolute PATH entry with statSync(candidate).isFile() inside a try/catch that skips on any throw. runPython (around lines 25-33) has no fallback to a bare "python" name, so when resolveInterpreter returns null it throws "No Python interpreter on PATH outside the task folder." The pre-change code used execFile("python"), which goes through CreateProcess PATH search. So if a Store App Execution Alias (APPEXECLINK reparse point) is the only python on PATH and stat fails on it, the python verification path now fails where it previously worked. The finding's regression claim is consistent with the code.

What I could not confirm: whether libuv's stat (statSync) really throws on APPEXECLINK stubs. I did not run anything, per the read-only rule, and I did not check the libuv source. The finding itself says it is not verified by execution. Also, the alias case is only a regression when the Store alias is functional (a real Store Python install), which is one common install layout.

Security impact: none. The failure is fail-closed (verification reports failure), the task-folder exclusion is untouched, and nothing is executed that was not previously executed. This is a functional regression, so LOW is the right severity. The proposed repair (lstatSync or accessSync X_OK as the existence test, while keeping the task-folder exclusion) is reasonable, but it should be checked with a real alias on Windows before it is treated as settled.

rows.title: failOperation() stops contained sessions outside stopsInFlight, so Host shutdown does not await their job termination
rows.reproduction: During Host shutdown in draining state, http.server.ts close() calls manager.failOperation(id) for each session (not manager.stop). failOperation calls this.sessions.get(id)?.stop() at manager.server.ts:321 directly, which runs containedSession.stop() -> terminateJob. That work is not added to stopsInFlight, so manager.settleStops() (http.server.ts ~line 966) does not await it. manager.dispose() and db.close() can run while the job is still being terminated. Termination then depends on kill-on-close at process exit. No DB write is lost, because failOperation's update happens before the await. The round-1 SHUT-1 repair is therefore partial.
rows.rootCause: Only manager.stop() registers its promise in stopsInFlight. failOperation and any other direct session.stop() caller bypass that registration.
rows.repair: Route session termination in failOperation through a helper that registers the promise in stopsInFlight (for example stopsInFlight.set(id, promise) around the session.stop() call), or register every session.stop() inside a single method that settleStops awaits.

votes.reasoning: The finding's reproduction omits the await at http.server.ts:948-961. In the draining path, close() runs manager.failOperation(id, ...) for every session inside Promise.allSettled and awaits it. failOperation (manager.server.ts:316-327) ends with `await this.sessions.get(id)?.stop()` at line 326, so job termination completes before the close() finally block runs `await ownedCleanup`, `await manager.settleStops()`, `manager.dispose()` (lines 964-968) and before db.close() (line 974). The race described (dispose or db.close running while the job is still terminating) does not occur on the shutdown path. The other branch (non-draining) calls manager.stop(), which is registered in stopsInFlight at manager.server.ts:1926-1928. The one remaining gap is a failOperation invoked from a background path (for example stopInBackground's failure handler at manager.server.ts:312) that is not awaited by close(). That is a narrow race in a failure path and not the stated defect, so the finding is refuted as written.

The finding's premise that shutdown does not await job termination on the failOperation path is wrong. In src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts close() (around lines 947-972), when containment.health.operationalState === "draining", every session is passed to manager.failOperation(id, ...) inside `await Promise.allSettled([...])`. That allSettled is awaited before the `finally` block that calls `await manager.settleStops()`, `manager.dispose()`, and before `db.close()`. So the failOperation promises, and the session.stop() call inside them (manager.server.ts ~line 321, `await this.sessions.get(id)?.stop()`), are awaited before the database closes, whether or not they are registered in stopsInFlight. The non-draining branch uses manager.stop(), which does register in stopsInFlight. Also, containedSession.stop() (adapters.server.ts ~392-395) awaits terminateJob(), which polls owned.terminate()/inspect() until ActiveProcesses reaches 0 or CONTAINMENT_CONFIRM_MS elapses (adapters.server.ts ~297-309), so the await spans kernel accounting. failOperation's early returns (TERMINAL state, or stopping.has(id), where the in-flight stop is already in stopsInFlight) do not leave an unawaited termination. The stopsInFlight-registration gap is real as a code-style asymmetry, but it has no observable consequence on the shutdown ordering the finding describes, so there is no defect.

rows.title: Unconfirmed-termination bookkeeping can throw inside the async termination chain and in the retry timer, leaving the stop promise unhandled and emptied unresolved
rows.reproduction: terminateJob's async IIFE calls owned.annotate, owned.close and owned.terminate, which all call persist() (writeFileSync plus renameSync). If persist throws (EPERM under a file lock), then: (a) at line ~312 the IIFE rejects before markEmpty(), so emptied never resolves and done never settles; (b) inside the retry closure at line 321 there is no try, so the throw is an uncaught timer exception, which the Host's uncaughtException containment treats as fatal; (c) stop() is invoked as 'void stop()' from group.onStop (line 345), so a rejection from terminateJob becomes an unhandled rejection. The recorded containment state stays 'terminating' or 'unconfirmed' with no event, and the job handle is never closed by this session.
rows.rootCause: Termination bookkeeping is not isolated from I/O failures. The only exception boundary is the caller, and the retry timer has none.
rows.repair: Wrap the body of terminateJob's IIFE and the retry closure in try/catch. On failure, record containment 'unconfirmed' in memory, emit provider.containment_unconfirmed with the error, keep the handle, and schedule another retry. Let markEmpty fire only on a confirmed zero. Make onStop call stop().catch(...) so rejections are contained.

votes.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the code; the defect is real but limited in impact. (1) adapters.server.ts terminateJob IIFE (about lines 300-325): owned.terminate() in the polling loop, owned.annotate(), and owned.close() are all unguarded. Each calls persist() (owned-process-group.server.ts:77-79: writeFileSync to .tmp then renameSync), and owned-process-group.server.ts:203-212 and :212 show terminate and annotate call persist directly. A throw therefore rejects the IIFE before markEmpty(), so `emptied` never resolves, the containment state stays 'terminating' or 'unconfirmed', and the handle is never closed by the session. (2) The retry closure (about line 321) calls owned.terminate() and owned.close() with no try, so the throw is an uncaught timer exception. failure.server.ts:152 and :447 treat uncaughtException as HOST_FATAL, and classifyFailure maps HOST_FATAL to CONTROLLED_EXIT. (3) stop() is invoked as `void stop()` from group.onStop (adapters.server.ts about line 345), so a rejection becomes an unhandled rejection. Under failure.server.ts:152 that is also HOST_FATAL when ownedAndSafe is false. Mitigating facts: this needs a write or rename failure on the record file (for example Windows EPERM from a file lock). The uncaught path ends in a controlled Host exit, and that exit closes the KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job, so members are still killed rather than orphaned. The main done path does reject rather than hang, because it awaits terminateJob directly. The failure is in bookkeeping and crash behavior, not a containment bypass. LOW is the right severity. The proposed repair is sound.

The core defect is real but narrower than the finding states. Verified in the code:

1. The bookkeeping calls are not isolated. terminateJob's async IIFE (adapters.server.ts ~L70-100) calls owned.annotate, owned.close, owned.terminate and settle/markEmpty. Each of these reaches persist() in owned-process-group.server.ts:77-80 (writeFileSync plus renameSync, no try/catch). The IIFE has no try/catch, so a throw before markEmpty() rejects `ending`, and emptied never resolves.

2. The retry closure (~L92-99) has no try. owned.terminate() calls persist() (owned-process-group.server.ts:206), so a throw inside retry() is an uncaught timer exception. That reaches process.on("uncaughtException") in failure.server.ts:570, which classifyFailure maps to HOST_FATAL / CONTROLLED_EXIT (failure.server.ts:152). A transient EPERM/EBUSY on the .tmp rename, from AV or an indexer holding the record file, can therefore take down the Host.

3. The onStop path is also real. group.onStop(() => { void stop(); }) (L345) discards the promise from stop(), which awaits terminateJob. The owned-processes group-stop loop (owned-processes.server.ts:36) calls these stops, so a rejection becomes an unhandled rejection.

Corrections to the finding: done does not hang. In the main path and the stop path, done awaits the same rejected `ending` (`await terminateJob(...)` before `await emptied`), so done rejects rather than staying pending. Only the emptied promise stays pending, and nothing else awaits it.

Containment: the failure is fail-closed. The record stays in 'terminating' or 'unconfirmed', the handle is never closed by the session, and a Host exit closes the KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE handle and so kills the job. Restart reconciliation treats unknown-birth or live records as possibly alive. No survivor escapes and no false "empty" is recorded. The issue is a controlled Host exit or a rejected session after a disk/lock error, which fits LOW. It is not a bypass, and it needs a filesystem error on the record path.

reviews.summary: Read-only review of native/bunny-owned-process.c after the round-1 and round-2 changes. The interactive stdin path, the writer-thread failure ordering, close_group and terminate_group, the handle-ownership and membership checks, and the write/endInput export checks (group identity by list membership and env, closed-group refusal, budget arithmetic) found no HIGH or MEDIUM defect and no bypass. Three LOW findings remain.

rows.title: inspect silently drops live job members it cannot open or verify
rows.reproduction: A job member whose OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) fails (transient access error, or a process that refuses the query) hits `if(!p)continue;` at line 219 and is omitted from the members array with no marker. The same silent omission happens at line 220 when IsProcessInJob fails: `IsProcessInJob(...)&&member` treats a call failure identically to 'not a member'. The snapshot therefore reports a reduced members list while activeProcesses (line 205) still counts the member. JS merges only the reported members into record.members (owned-process-group.server.ts:191), and restart reconciliation builds its expected identities solely from record.members (manager.server.ts:236). A member absent from record.members is never checked after a Host restart, so reconciliation can conclude every recorded identity is absent while an unrecorded member is alive.
rows.rootCause: Enumeration failures are treated as 'no member' rather than as an incomplete inspection. The C2 split of IsProcessInJob failure from non-member, applied in launch (line 161-162), was not carried into inspect. The snapshot has no field recording how many members could not be verified.
rows.repair: Count members skipped by OpenProcess failure and by IsProcessInJob failure (separately from confirmed non-members) and return them as an extra field such as unverifiedMembers. In JS, treat unverifiedMembers > 0 as an incomplete identity set: mark the record for review and do not treat absence of the recorded identities as a complete picture. Alternatively retry the open once before skipping.

votes.reasoning: The omission itself is real. native/bunny-owned-process.c:219 (`if(!p)continue;`) drops a member whose OpenProcess fails with no marker, and line 220 (`IsProcessInJob(...)&&member`) treats an IsProcessInJob call failure the same as a non-member. activeProcesses (line 205) still counts the member, and the snapshot has no unverified count. JS merges only reported members (owned-process-group.server.ts:191), and restart reconciliation builds expected identities only from record.members (manager.server.ts:236). This contradicts the RESTART-01 comment in manager.server.ts ("none is silently dropped"). The stated harm is largely prevented elsewhere. The job is created with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and no breakaway (line 137), so when the previous Host dies and its last job handle closes, the kernel ends every remaining member. A member that is alive after restart and absent from record.members therefore requires a kernel invariant to fail. Members also accumulate across snapshots (line 191), so an omission needs every inspection to fail for that PID. The live Stop and containment paths use kernel ActiveProcesses, not the members list, so they are unaffected. Remaining impact is diagnostic under-reporting. LOW is justified; the repair (an unverifiedMembers count routed to review) is reasonable but not a containment bypass.

The silent omission is real. native/bunny-owned-process.c:216-219 does `if(!p)continue;` after OpenProcess with no marker, and lines 220-222 treat an IsProcessInJob failure the same as "not a member" (`IsProcessInJob(...)&&member`). activeProcesses (line 205) comes from JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation and still counts the omitted member, so the snapshot's members list can be smaller than activeProcesses. The JS side has no check for that mismatch: owned-process-group.server.ts:190-191 merges only the reported members, and the merge is additive, so a member is lost only if it first appears in a snapshot where its open fails.

The claimed survivor consequence does not hold. rows.title: Prompt writer ResumeThread result ignored after the root is running
rows.reproduction: launch() resumes the root at line 176 (the last point where a failure is reported as a refused launch), then calls `if(g->writer)ResumeThread(g->writer);` at line 177 with the return value discarded. If that resume fails, the root runs and blocks on stdin forever, the prompt is never delivered, and launch returns a successful handle, so the session appears started and is reported as running instead of refused. The round-2 L4 claim that every native failure precedes the root running holds only for the root resume, not for this one.
rows.rootCause: The writer resume is treated as infallible after the root has started. Its failure has no handler and no containment record update.
rows.repair: Check the return value of ResumeThread(g->writer). On failure, close the group (close_group(g) kills the root and the job) and fail the launch, or resume the writer before ResumeThread(pi.hThread) so a failure is still a pre-run refusal. Pick one ordering and document it in native/README.md.

rows.title: Interactive input budget undercounts bytes delivered before a partial write failure
rows.reproduction: write_input_owned loops WriteFile over the buffer (line 237). Bytes already in the pipe are not charged to MAX_INTERACTIVE_INPUT, so the per-group budget can be exceeded by up to one write's worth of bytes across retries. Practical impact is small because a failed WriteFile on this pipe usually means the reader closed, so later writes fail too.

rows.repair: Charge each WriteFile result immediately: `g->inputWritten+=written;` inside the while loop, before the failure check. Keep the pre-call check at line 235 as it is.

The telemetry path is cached and runs once per Host process, so it is less exposed than the processTable path. rows.title: Host-side bare powershell.exe/taskkill.exe run unowned with the Host cwd, which can be an approved task folder
rows.reproduction: Preconditions: (a) the Host is started from a folder that is also an approved project/task folder (e.g. the repo root, which is what the dev workflow does; http.server.ts:279 sets TaskManager root = options.root ?? process.cwd(), and manager.server.ts:790 allows folder === defaultRoot as a task working directory); (b) a provider task has that folder as its cwd, so it can write files there. Steps: the provider writes a PE named powershell.exe (any compiled binary, or a copy of a program) into the Host cwd. The Host then calls processTable() (process-tree.server.ts:11, via execOwnedFile with no cwd, called from manager.server.ts lines 248, 1770, 1832, 1932, 1946, 1967 during stop/reconcile/launch-survivor checks) or the telemetry GPU probe (telemetry.server.ts:57, runs once per Host process at startup), or a computer.* action (computer.server.ts:393). libuv resolves a bare executable name by searching the child cwd before PATH on Windows, so the planted file runs as the Host user, outside any Bunny-owned Job Object (execOwnedFile only calls trackOwnedChild, which is bookkeeping, not containment). The same applies to stopOwnedChildren() at owned-processes.server.ts:43-44, which runs bare taskkill.exe with the Host cwd during shutdown. The planted program can also print a fabricated process table on stdout, which feeds the survivor and identity logic in manager.server.ts.
rows.rootCause: Windows bare-name resolution for execFile/spawn with no explicit cwd or absolute path uses the Host's current directory first. Several Host-side Windows launches pass a bare name ('powershell.exe', 'taskkill.exe') and no cwd, and the execOwnedFile/trackOwnedChild helper does not put them in a job. The F04 repair covered provider, verification, and mission-process launches, but not these Host-side helper launches. Provider and mission launches resolve absolute paths (discovery.server.ts searchPath, process.server.ts onPath/realpath), so they are not affected. Only these bare-name callers are.
rows.repair: Launch Windows helpers by absolute System32 path (join(process.env.SystemRoot ?? 'C:\\Windows', 'System32','WindowsPowerShell','v1.0','powershell.exe') and join(SystemRoot,'System32','taskkill.exe')), and set an explicit cwd outside any project folder (e.g. the Host data directory). Ideally route them through runWindowsOwnedProcess so they are owned. Add a static test that no win32 execFile/spawn call in src passes a bare executable name without an absolute path or a non-writable cwd. Impact is limited to a Host where cwd is a provider-writable folder, so a note that Host cwd must not be a task folder would also reduce exposure.

reviews.summary: Read-only review of the F04 containment diff against the truthfulness and live-code-visibility lens. Found four real issues. A persisted restart task error asserts provider processes 'ended' before any identity check. Provider probes are live contained jobs that liveCodeExecutions cannot see. Records with no identity are listed for review only once and are then silently dropped. An unreadable-record hold is released without reconciling that record. Stop wording also says the job 'was terminated' while termination is unconfirmed. No bypass of the F01 hold was found for verification.* jobs, sessions, survivors or restart survivors (access undefined classifies as live).

rows.title: Restart task error asserts provider processes ended before identities are checked
rows.reproduction: Host A runs a Codex task in a Windows job and dies while a member is still alive. Host B starts. The restart walk (manager.server.ts ~lines 164-186) calls this.update(task,{state:'failed', error:'...Windows job-contained provider processes ended with the previous Host (kill-on-close); this Host killed no process.'},'task.failed'). Startup then calls reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions (~line 189), which emits provider_session.interrupted ('Verifying recorded process identities before this counts as stopped') and, if an identity is still alive, provider_session.cleanup_unconfirmed ('are still alive ... treated as live code'). The persisted task error and the later events contradict each other, and the task error is what the task card shows.
rows.rootCause: The restart walk writes an unverified 'ended' claim into the persisted task error. The corroboration happens afterwards and is never reflected in that text.
rows.repair: Reword the task error to state only what is known, e.g. 'Host restarted while a provider job was running; the previous Host's job handle closed, so the kernel ends its members. Recorded processes are being verified; this Host killed no process.' Better still, drop the 'ended' claim from the task error and let provider_session.* events carry the verdict.

So the persisted task error asserts "ended" as fact while the later events say the verdict is still pending or contradicted.

It does not check whether the task had a job record. adapters.server.ts:206 uses plain spawn unless win32 and the default spawnChild, so tasks without a job still receive the "Windows job-contained ... ended" text. The harm is a misleading card/error string. It conflicts with the STOP-3 repair (truthful stop text), so it is a truthfulness regression, but LOW is the justified severity.

Gate any job wording on the presence of a job record. Let provider_session.* events carry the verdict.

This is written before reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions (line 185) runs. Reconcile (lines 225-265) explicitly treats the outcome as unverified ("Verifying recorded process identities before this counts as stopped"), and can emit cleanup_unconfirmed with "still alive ... treated as live code". The finding's stated reproduction is largely unreachable, though. A member of a KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job cannot survive the last job handle closing, and the Host's death closes that handle, so "dies while a member is still alive" holds only if a member escaped the job or the old Host is still running. Neither is the normal case. Escape is not shown in the code reviewed: native/bunny-owned-process.c:137 sets KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE with no breakaway, and on win32 production launches go through containedSession (adapters.server.ts:206). The non-contained paths are the spawnChild test seam and non-win32 code, which are out of the Windows contract.

What survives is a real overclaim: the same unverified "ended" sentence is applied unconditionally to every interrupted task, including tasks in "launching" (possibly no job created) and "verifying" tasks that may not have a provider-session record, so the claim is asserted without evidence for those tasks. Because the authoritative verdict lives in the provider_session.* events and the claim is true in the normal kernel-guaranteed case, I rate it LOW rather than MEDIUM. rows.title: Provider probes are live contained jobs invisible to liveCodeExecutions

rows.title: Records with no identity are listed for review only once, then silently dropped
rows.reproduction: Restart 1: a provider record with no recorded identity is marked by markProviderSessionReview (reviewRequired=true, closed=true) and a provider_session.cleanup_unverifiable event is emitted (manager.server.ts ~line 241). rows.title: Unreadable-record hold is released without reconciling the record

The 10 s check() calls readProviderSessions(dataDirectory).unreadable.includes(file). Once the file parses, check() deletes the lingering key and returns. Nothing feeds the recovered record into reconcileInterruptedProviderSessions, and no provider_session event is emitted on release. The record's identities are therefore not checked in this run.

Root-cause correction: the event text at line 214 says the hold lasts "until the record is readable or removed", so readability-release matches the text. The defect is the gap between that text and the reconciliation contract: a record released from the hold is never reconciled this run and gets no event.

A second effect, not in the finding: readProviderSessions (owned-process-group.server.ts:100-117) is not side-effect free. For each non-closed record it persists state 'interrupted' and closed=true (line 114). The check's readProviderSessions call therefore silently rewrites the record on the readable transition, while the record is discarded from the results. The record is still recovered on the next restart because its containment is not terminal, so the loss is in this run's accounting, not permanent.

Impact is limited. restartSurvivorRefusal (line 200-207) only consults restartSurvivorMission, which unreadable records never populate, so the hold never blocked launches for that work. The effect is that the live-code count drops with no process-table corroboration and no event. Kernel kill-on-close also makes a surviving member unlikely. That supports LOW, not a higher severity. It is not a documented out-of-contract class.
